title: Physically Constrained Problem-Independent Machine Learning (PIML) for Joint Prediction of Condensed Stiffness and Compliance Sensitivities in Topology Optimization
content: Learning condensed substructure stiffness accelerates analysis, but accurate stiffness values do not ensure material-monotone derivatives for compliance updates. Physically constrained problem-independent machine learning (PIML), termed PIML-S, addresses this mismatch by jointly predicting stiffness condensed under tensor-product first-order boundary interpolation and state-conditioned elemental sensitivities. Nonnegative energy allocation couples the sensitivities to the stiffness-predicted energy, replacing online fine-field recovery and differentiation of the stiffness network. Training uses local material fields and deformation samples rather than global optimization trajectories, enabling reuse across global geometries, supports and loads. Across four two-dimensional benchmarks exceeding one million elements each, complete optimization reaches speedups up to 10.57× over the fine-mesh finite element method (Fine FEM). Final compliances differ by less than 0.56% from those of the Fine FEM reference designs. On the two three-dimensional cases with Fine FEM references, complete optimizations give 192–261× speedups, with final Fine FEM compliance differences of 4.61–6.76%. Across all four three-dimensional cases, speedups over shape-function-based PIML are 2.01–3.58×. The two three-dimensional benchmarks exceeding one million cells have endpoint compliance differences below 0.13% relative to analytical-substructure optimization references. A perforated plate with 62.41 million analysis cells is optimized in 40.44 min on a laptop with 32 GB of memory. By replacing mode-dependent recovery with scalar energy queries, the framework strengthens PIML acceleration as local deformation spaces grow and makes high-resolution three-dimensional optimization accessible on memory-limited hardware.
